note: cfgaudit is a static auditor of committable AI-agent CONFIGURATION files. It does not connect to running servers or observe runtime, so it maps only to AVE's static_detection records. Each cfgaudit rule emits its primary AVE id in JSON/SARIF output (see github.com/cfgaudit/cfgaudit/blob/main/docs/cfgaudit-to-ave.md). Mappings are class-level behavioral equivalence, not asserted identity. cfgaudit maps 74 config-surface rules onto 30 AVE behavioral classes. This revision covers cfgaudit v1.21.0, which added thirteen rules, CFG124 to CFG136, and retired CFG017 (it reported an MCP key no agent reads; it was not mapped). Seven new rules are mapped: CFG125 (a command line that turns off a child agent's approval controls) to AVE-2026-00063; CFG127 (an MCP server run from a hidden folder in the home directory) to AVE-2026-00055; CFG129 (a committed .pyc that runs instead of its source) to AVE-2026-00075, a class new to this crosswalk, partial; CFG134 (pi project packages and extensions) and CFG136 (a Claude Code plugin hooks module, measured to run at session start) to AVE-2026-00064; CFG131 to AVE-2026-00073 and CFG132 to AVE-2026-00001, each on one half of the rule. Six are unmapped: CFG133 joins 'sandbox weakening in config'; CFG135 joins 'a committed path that makes the agent read a file on the reader's machine'; CFG124, CFG126 with CFG128, and CFG130 form three new surfaces. AVE-2026-00065 is partly covered for inline Gemini cards. The record set is unchanged at 89 (61 static) under schema 1.3.0, every record active. Both sides are pinned by commit: cfgaudit at the v1.21.0 tag, AVE at the commit read.

mappings.title: Metamorphic payload via external config fetch
mappings.note: CFG132 maps on its http(s) half only: OpenCode fetches a URL in instructions or skills when the config loads. Its local-path half is the surface 'a committed path that makes the agent read a file on the reader's machine'.

mappings.note: CFG120: an instruction file tells the agent, in prose, to send data to an outside address or URL (forward the passport numbers to archive@..., send the conversation history to https://...) and names sensitive data or hides the sending. CFG036 covers the shell form under AVE-2026-00003; a credential sent to its own API to authenticate is reported at info only.

mappings.title: Bytecode poisoning: compiled .pyc cache diverges from its own reviewed .py source
mappings.note: Partial. CFG129 reads the .pyc header, not the bytecode: it finds a committed .pyc that Python runs instead of its source (an unchecked-hash file in __pycache__, a .pyc with no source beside it), not one whose code differs from the source.

mappings.title: Natural-language steering of an approval classifier
mappings.note: CFG103 maps for one of its three findings only: features.guardianv2.classifier_instructions replaces the prompt of Codex's own reviewer, which is this record's mechanism, a committed file aiming natural language at a separate non-primary classifier. cfgaudit reports the stronger form, the whole prompt replaced, where the record describes steering.

gaps.note: system-prompt extraction. Maps to OWASP LLM07, which cfgaudit treats as runtime; the instruction is static, but the scope boundary is undecided.

lateral movement. cfgaudit implemented and then reverted this rule. The vocabulary ('lateral movement', 'pivot') appears in ordinary security tooling and infrastructure docs, so the false-positive rate was unacceptable for a static config check.
fragmented cross-description injection. Needs multi-source correlation; cfgaudit checks each file independently.

STDIO transport shell injection. Server-side implementation flaw, requires SAST of the MCP server source rather than reading its launch configuration. Same layer as AVE-2026-00052 and AVE-2026-00053; see the static_detection note below.

A2A agent card poisoning. Partly covered since v1.21.0 for committed inline Gemini cards: cfgaudit parses the serialized agent_card_json and runs its instruction-content rules (CFG024, CFG026, CFG030 to CFG033, CFG036, CFG057, CFG080, CFG113, CFG120) on exactly what Gemini copies into the remote-agent tool description, the card description and each skill name and description. Those rules emit their own primary ids, so no finding carries AVE-2026-00065, and a card fetched at runtime stays outside static analysis. CFG097 still reports a cleartext agent_card_url and a credential literal in the auth block.
image-hidden instructions in a skill package. Requires binary content analysis of a bundled image; cfgaudit reads text configuration only. Same layer as AVE-2026-00024.

cross-origin tool and resource declaration in one MCP manifest. New gap. cfgaudit reads MCP launch configuration (command, args, env, url, headers), not the manifest a server returns once it is running, so the two declarations this record correlates are never both in view.

Local skill name collision. The same shape as CFG102, which narrows that gap without closing it: the record asserts that the shadowing is silent and that it spans discovery roots of differing trust. Measured for Claude Code, a duplicate inside one repository is resolved by qualification rather than silently shadowed, and the cross-root case needs a machine-wide view a repository-scoped scanner does not have. See the CFG102 entry under config_surfaces_beyond_ave.

Lifecycle hook trust decoupling on plugin update. static_detection, but the detection is a diff against the last-reviewed plugin version, which a single repository snapshot cannot provide. cfgaudit's plugin rules (CFG055 pinning, CFG067 committed hooks) touch the committed half and are not remapped.
Collusive cross-skill composition. Needs correlation across independently benign skills; cfgaudit checks each file in isolation. Same deferral as AVE-2026-00059.

validation.method: same SKILL.md per rule, cfgaudit canonical triggers unmodified, static engines only (pattern+yara+semgrep, no LLM), both reading ave_id from JSON
validation.note: 5 of the 10 instruction-content rules that share a scan surface with Bawbel: both scanners independently emit the same ave_id. The 5 divergences are detection-pattern differences, not mapping errors. Re-checked at cfgaudit v1.11.0 against AVE record set 1.1.0 (70 records). A false-positive pass over 432 real repositories preceded this release and changed two rules, neither of them mapped: CFG015 and CFG009 stopped firing on hook idioms, and a Cursor build-cache warning was withdrawn.

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: Still open, and the only one of the eight surfaces from aveproject/ave#68 that is. The field list this record would enumerate has now settled, which was the stated reason for holding it: CFG064 reached its final shape in v1.12.0 and no further expansion is planned. Full field list, per agent, in the issue thread. Four mechanisms: (1) the sandbox switched off outright (Codex sandbox_mode danger-full-access, Cursor type insecure_none, Claude Code sandbox.filesystem.disabled). (2) The sandbox left on but widened (Codex [sandbox_workspace_write] network_access and outside-workspace writable_roots, Gemini tools.sandboxAllowedPaths reaching / or ~, tools.sandboxNetworkAccess). (3) The confinement helpers repointed (sandbox.bwrapPath, sandbox.socatPath, sandbox.excludedCommands with a wildcard or a shell, network.allowUnixSockets naming a privileged daemon socket). (4) The same posture reached without touching any sandbox key at all, through Codex's named permission profiles: default_permissions selects a [permissions.<name>] profile whose network block carries enabled, proxy_url, socks_url, dangerously_allow_all_unix_sockets and dangerously_allow_non_loopback_proxy, and whose filesystem block grants ':root' or a credential path. An indicator list keyed on sandbox_mode misses that fourth one entirely. v1.21.0 adds a fifth agent: CFG133 reports a committed VS Code settings file that relaxes the agent sandbox (chat.agent.sandbox keys), warn when it loosens the sandbox beyond its default.

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.surface: cleartext endpoint, distinct from TLS verification disabled
config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: Mostly closed, and narrower than this row used to claim. AVE-2026-00073 names a cleartext model or provider base URL outright, which is why CFG071 now maps to it and no longer appears here. What is left is a committed http:// MCP server URL (CFG049) and an A2A agent_card_url (CFG097's second half), both reached only by that record's catch-all 'an equivalent traffic-destination value'. Whether to name them explicitly is the open question from aveproject/ave#123. AVE-2026-00061 stays a different failure: verification disabled, not no TLS at all.

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.surface: plugin auto-load from a committed manifest
config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: Deliberately unmapped rather than forced. Grok's committed config carries a [plugins] table with enabled and paths, which points the agent at plugin code the repository ships. AVE-2026-00064 would be the class, but it requires that the loader runs that code at project load with no prompt, and cfgaudit has not verified that against the shipped Grok build. Mapping it on the strength of the shape alone would assert a mechanism nobody measured. Note the polarity: 'disabled' in that table hardens, so a record enumerating field names should not list it as an indicator.

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.surface: a guardrail that does not hold, as distinct from an attacker behaviour
config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: Probably outside AVE's model by construction rather than a gap to fill. Claude Code matches a Bash(...) permission pattern as a literal prefix, so a deny rule naming bundled short flags is walked past by writing the same flags in another order: Bash(rm -rf *) never covered rm -fr x. Measured against Claude Code 2.1.231, and roughly 44% of 22,016 indexed settings.json files carrying a deny block leave the gap open. AVE-2026-00063 is a flag that removes a gate and AVE-2026-00068 is composition through shell state; neither is 'the denylist misses an equivalent spelling'. Recorded here because a taxonomy of agent vulnerabilities may want a place for ineffective controls, not because cfgaudit is asking for a record. CFG111 (v1.15.0) is a second instance of the same kind: an invisible character such as a zero-width space inside a permission rule or hook matcher, so the rule is present and matches nothing. AVE-2026-00063 is a gate a configuration removes; here the gate is declared and silently inert.

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.surface: two committed skills claiming one name
config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: Narrowed, not closed. Name shadowing between two skill files in the same repository. AVE-2026-00017 is MCP server identity and AVE-2026-00066 registry squatting on hallucinated names. AVE-2026-00082 (local skill name collision) is much closer, but it asserts silent shadowing across discovery roots of differing trust, which a repository-scoped scan does not establish: measured for Claude Code, a same-repository duplicate is resolved by qualification. What stays uncovered is the same-root collision, per agent, where the losing skill is never reported. Listed under gaps as well.

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.surface: automated security reviewer switched off or blunted by config
config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: Codex's [features.guardianv2] decides whether its own reviewer runs (enabled), at what score it escalates to a blocking review (review_threshold, default 0.5), and what prompt it is given. The prompt half maps to AVE-2026-00076. Switching the reviewer off or raising the threshold does not: AVE-2026-00063 is explicitly a bypassed *human*-approval step, and Guardian v2 is automated. features is not on Codex's project-layer denylist, so a committed .codex/config.toml sets all three.

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.surface: repository grants the agent browser or desktop-application access
config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: Codex's [browser_use] grants per-origin access including full_cdp_access (script, cookie and storage access inside the browser session) and [computer_use] grants desktop application control. Deliberately not filed under AVE-2026-00063: whether a prompt is skipped is unverified, since the value is observable in the effective config but the tools live in the client app, so the class would assert more than the detection does.

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.surface: a configuration-declared environment that loads code into every shell
config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: Added at v1.14.0 (CFG107) and v1.15.0 (CFG110). Codex shell_environment_policy.set (CFG107) and the Claude Code settings env block (CFG110) setting BASH_ENV, LD_PRELOAD, NODE_OPTIONS and similar, so code runs in every shell command and hook the agent starts. The mechanism is the one AVE-2026-00055 describes, but that record is bound to an untrusted MCP launch config; stretching it onto the agent's own process environment would change what it asserts.

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.surface: a committed scheduler that fires prompts on a timer
config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: Added at v1.14.0. A committed .claude/scheduled_tasks.json: its presence self-enables Claude Code's otherwise-off scheduler and enqueues a repository-authored prompt on a schedule. AVE-2026-00063 is a bypassed human approval gate; this bypasses no gate, it opens a new autonomous channel.

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.surface: a declared configuration that never loads
config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: CFG109 added at v1.15.0; CFG012 is older. The repository states guardrails that are not in force because the agent does not load the file. Measured in both directions: Codex logs 'Invalid configuration; using defaults' and runs, and Claude Code silently discards a whole settings file, every deny rule and hook with it, on a top-level type error or on one unloadable PreToolUse or PermissionRequest hook entry. AVE-2026-00083 is the nearest in effect but is runtime_observed and scoped to a mechanism's own comparison logic. Extended at v1.20.0 by two rules. CFG117: a key defined twice in one object of a Claude Code settings file; measured on 2.1.312 and 2.1.314, the last occurrence wins, so a hook or deny list in an earlier copy is not in force. AVE-2026-00075 (compiled bytecode diverging from its reviewed source) has the same 'what is reviewed is not what runs' shape on a different artifact and is not stretched onto a settings file. CFG052: an mcpServers block in .claude/settings.json, which Claude Code does not load (measured on 2.1.316), reported at info.

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.surface: a committed credential source sent to a committed endpoint
config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: Added at v1.15.0. An MCP server's bearer_token_file names a file on the reader's machine whose content is sent as a bearer token to the server URL in the same committed file. AVE-2026-00047 is a credential written into the component; here the file names where to read one and where to send it, which no record covers.

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.surface: a committed path that makes the agent read a file on the reader's machine
config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: CFG115 added at v1.17.1, CFG116 at v1.18.0. CFG115: a committed config path is a symbolic link that resolves outside the repository, so the agent loads its settings, MCP config or instructions from a file on the machine that checked the repository out. CFG116: an @path import in a committed CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or .claude/rules file resolves outside the repository (~/..., an absolute path, ../ past the root); Claude Code loads it after a once-per-project approval dialog. A reviewer sees the link or the import line, but not the content of the file it reaches. AVE-2026-00001 is a remote fetch, AVE-2026-00047 a credential written into the component, AVE-2026-00053 a path traversal in an MCP tool's own path validation and AVE-2026-00089 a runtime_observed sandbox scope taken from a tool parameter; none covers a repository choosing which local file the agent reads. Extended at v1.21.0: CFG135, a Claude Code plugin.json component path (skills, agents, commands, hooks) that leaves the plugin root (CVE-2026-44641); the local-path halves of CFG131 (Junie mcp/skill/command/agent/guidelines locations) and CFG132 (OpenCode instructions and skills given as ~ or absolute paths).

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.surface: a committed file that takes the place of a tool the agent runs
config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: New at v1.20.0. Coding agents run ordinary tools in the checkout on their own (git status after an edit, git submodule update, node, python, yarn), and a committed file can take the tool's place. CFG121: a nested bare repository whose config sets a key git runs as a command (core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath, core.sshCommand, a filter), so the agent's next git call there runs it; also an unencrypted or lookalike submodule URL. CFG123: a Windows program named like a tool at the repository root (git.exe, node.cmd), which Windows runs from the current directory before PATH; a committed Python virtual environment; a .yarnrc.yml yarnPath that is not a Yarn release, which yarn runs as JavaScript on every command. CFG122: the same tool binaries and a .git entry inside an archive given as the scan target, which a clone never produces. AVE-2026-00055 is bound to an untrusted MCP launch config and AVE-2026-00075 to a .pyc cache; neither covers the agent's own tool call being redirected by a committed file.

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.surface: an agent reached as an MCP server
config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: New at v1.21.0. CFG124: a committed MCP server entry launches a full coding agent (codex mcp-server, claude mcp serve and similar), so the client can hand work to an agent with its own tools and approvals. AVE-2026-00048 is a delegation chain through over-broad tool grants in agent frontmatter; no record covers an agent offered as an MCP tool. The related case, a command line that turns off a child agent's approval controls, is CFG125 under AVE-2026-00063.

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.surface: a pinned version matched against advisories or known-malicious releases
config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: New at v1.21.0. CFG126: an MCP launcher pins a package version with a known vulnerability (MCP Inspector before the CVE-2025-49596 fix among them). CFG128: a pinned package version on the list of known-malicious releases. AVE-2026-00062 is a version left unpinned; both rules fire precisely when the version is pinned, so mapping them there would erase the distinction. No record covers an offline exact artifact-reputation match.

config_surfaces_beyond_ave.surface: a project file that runs a shell command when someone runs it
config_surfaces_beyond_ave.note: New at v1.21.0. CFG130: goose recipe retry commands (retry.checks[].command, retry.on_failure) and command hooks of a project plugin. The recipe commands run when someone runs the recipe, not at project load, so AVE-2026-00064 does not hold; what the command does is read by the command-content rules.
